settling.interpretation: An engineering settling gate comparing the last two 90-second warmup blocks, not proof of stationarity. Limits are fixed before execution; failing histories remain visible and are not replaced.

methods.raw_composition: Full-covariance MEWMA of complete measured CPU shares in an information-preserving orthonormal contrast basis.
methods.ilr_composition: The same full-covariance MEWMA of complete ILR coordinates.

reference_definition: Integrate native CPU-time increments over the reference interval, close the resulting vector, and fix it before monitoring. Store total CPU separately. No quota, intervention label or external outcome enters either detector.
calibration: Background repetitions 1-2 fit means/full covariances. Repetitions 3-5 set each threshold to the empirical higher 95th percentile of whole-history maximum scores. With twelve planned calibration histories this is the maximum; the small calibration set cannot guarantee a 5% test rate. Freeze before starting any test job.
load: One k6 process and persistent virtual users per fresh-stack history, continuously through warmup, reference, guards and monitoring. Checkout uses constant arrival rate; advertising retains constant concurrency so actual ad throughput is separately recorded, not asserted constant.
comparison: Twenty fresh-runner test pairs, one gradual reallocation and one unchanged-control history per runner, with deterministic balanced order. Compare known-intervention detection and delay on common qualified pairs; control signals describe behavior without intervention, not automatically false alarms.
quality: Require positive finite CPU values and at least 95% counter coverage for every service, exact quota readbacks, timely updates and passed settling gate for both histories in a primary pair. External SLO failures never exclude a history. Preserve all nonqualifying histories and diagnostics. Retry only technical job failures, preserving attempt IDs.
scope: Observe relative runtime state and test detection timing, not SLO prediction, a safety-boundary estimator, or a new MEWMA algorithm.
